definition: Trustworthy AI refers to artificial intelligence systems that are designed to have transparent reasoning, are explainable (XAI), accountable, robust, fair and honest, respectful of data privacy, and steerable or alignable with human goals.
details: Trustworthy AI refers to artificial intelligence systems that are designed to have transparent reasoning, are explainable (XAI), accountable, robust, fair and honest, respectful of data privacy, and steerable or alignable with human goals.

explainer.lead: Trustworthy AI is the goal of building systems whose reasoning is transparent, explainable, accountable, robust, fair, honest, privacy-respecting and steerable toward human goals. It matters because deployment decisions hinge on whether people can understand, challenge and correct a system.

tiers.eli5: It is a checklist for a machine you would trust to help run something important: it shows its work, plays fair, keeps secrets, and does what you ask.
tiers.practitioner: Teams operationalise it as audits, documentation and constraints layered onto models rather than a single property baked into weights. A common pitfall is treating a feature like explainability as sufficient while ignoring robustness or alignment gaps.
tiers.paperLevel: There is no single formal definition: it is a conjunction of properties (transparency, explainability, accountability, robustness, fairness, honesty, privacy, steerability/alignability) each with its own metrics. Known limit: these properties can conflict, and satisfying all simultaneously is not guaranteed.

explainer.example: A loan-screening model ships with per-decision explanations, fairness testing across groups, and a human review path so applicants can contest outcomes.
